text: Koichi Mizushima (水島公一, Mizushima Kōichi; born January 30, 1941) is a Japanese researcher recognized for discovering lithium cobalt oxide (LiCoO2) and related materials used in lithium-ion batteries (Li-ion battery). He was trained as a physicist at the University of Tokyo and earned a PhD in Physics from the same institution. He spent 13 years working in the Physics Department at the University of Tokyo. In 1977, he was invited by Professor John Goodenough from the Inorganic Chemistry Department at Oxford University to join as a research scientist. During his tenure at Oxford from 1977 to 1979, Dr. Mizushima, in collaboration with John B. Goodenough, discovered LiCoO2 and related compounds now utilized in the cathode of the Li-ion battery.[1][2][3] After his time at Oxford, he joined Toshiba.[4]
